notes: PARENTAGE CORRECTED (research 2026-07-03): the export makes Isaac a son of John Albertson (1771-1842) & Ann Pine — REFUTED: the 1897 Biographical Review states Chalkley (b. Jan 1816) was the youngest of that couple's ten children, and Ann was ~49 in 1824. Isaac is almost certainly their GRANDSON: probable parents JOSIAH ALBERTSON (1795-1849, I182197730739) & ABIGAIL C. HODSON (m. Haddonfield MM 21 Mar 1822 — 'Josiah (s John and Ann)' to Abigail, d. Thomas and Mary Hodson). Evidence: marriage timing fits an 1824 eldest child; the couple had children of exactly this cohort in this county (Craig: 'Mary Ann ALBERTSON (d. Josiah & Abigail)' m. 1853); geography matches (Haddonfield/Centre Twp); middle initial 'J' plausibly = Josiah. Confidence: probable, not yet documented — confirm via the 1850 census household of widow Abigail, Isaac's 1896 NJ death return, or the Camden Co. surrogate file.

Wife Mary Ann Shone (b. ~1829): Shone family confirmed in Camden Co. records (Craig's clerk's marriages, incl. Thomas J. Shone m. 1853 to Sarah Jane PINE — same Pine family circle). Isaac's own marriage record not found in Craig — possibly Gloucester Co. or pre-registration.

No credible Civil War service: he was 37-40 in 1861; the one 'Isaac Albertson' in Stryker's NJ roster and the Hatch Post G.A.R. list are unproven identities — treat as NOT a veteran absent pension/muster proof.

Geography: 'Snow Hill' (later Lawnside) and the ancestral Albertson homestead at Greenland/Magnolia were both in Centre Township; in 1880 Isaac lived roughly a mile from the family farm then held by his uncle Chalkley's branch — a cadet branch farming next door.
